iterations.targetCluster: commercial lead-type queries (aged mortgage leads, aged insurance leads, final expense leads, iul leads)

expected.basis: 629 views/mo across the top four lead-type pages converting at ~0.95% today. Modelling C at 5% — 8x below the provider page's measured 43.33% — gives ~31 clicks vs 6, i.e. +25/mo on a 69-click base. A hypothesis to test, not a forecast: intent on a guide page is genuinely lower than on a provider review, and the gap will not fully close.

at2w.correctionOf: An earlier reading the same day concluded 'redistribution, not creation' and set the verdict to do-not-extend. That was wrong, and it was wrong for a specific reason worth recording: it measured ONLY store-side sessions, because the site-side denominator was believed unreadable after GA4 528489903 returned 403. The 403 is real but it only affects the local MCP's OAuth identity. Production reads that exact property fine through the WIF service account brsg-analytics-reader@brsg-mcp, and the site's own /api/reports/outbound-clicks endpoint serves the per-page views and clicks. The denominator was one authenticated request away the whole time.
at2w.note: The hypothesis was that a hero door would lift conversion on lead-type pages from 0.95% to ~5%. Measured 7.24% on the four target pages - the bet BEAT its own conservative case. Critically, absolute clicks rose 6 -> 22 while views FELL 629 -> 304, so this is not a shrinking-denominator artifact: the pages did more with half the traffic. Site-wide affiliate clicks rose 69 -> 86 (+25%) over the same collapse.
at2w.theTension: Site-side clicks rose 25% but store-side sessions rose only 10% (49 -> 54). Two scoreboards, two answers. Commission is computed store-side, so the store number is the one that pays - but the site number is the one that isolates whether a design change worked. Track both and never quote one as the other. Part of the gap is the provider page giving back share: 39 clicks / 43.33% before, 28 clicks / 35.44% now.
at2w.theRealHeadline: Lead-type page views fell 629 -> 304 in two weeks, a >50% traffic collapse, which is the crawl transition still biting. Conversion work is now clearly succeeding on a shrinking base. That does not argue against more conversion work; it argues that conversion alone cannot outrun the traffic loss.

iterations.notes: Both hero buttons on these pages were internal (/compare, /price-index), so the site's highest-traffic commercial pages had no affiliate path above the fold. The mid-page CtaBanner also passes buttonHref, which sets useAffiliate=false — it is an internal compare link sitting exactly where intent peaks. Added a deep-linked door as the primary hero action; compare and pricing keep their position as secondary. Deep links verified per page: mortgage-leads -> /mortgage-leads-purchase-refinance/, final-expense-leads -> /life-insurance-leads/. insurance-leads correctly falls back to /all-lead-types/ — the partner has no generic-insurance buy page and that mapping is deliberate (lib/affiliate.ts, confirmed by Bill 2026-08-06). Destinations re-verified: 200, zero redirects, real buy pages ('Aged Mortgage Leads', 'Buy Aged Life Insurance Leads for Agents — From $0.25'). rel=nofollow sponsored and disclosure present on every instance. Measure via utm_content=hero-door. MEASURED 2026-09-01 (corrected): the door WORKED and beat its own hypothesis - 0.95% -> 7.24% on the four target pages, 6 -> 22 absolute clicks against a halving of traffic. An earlier same-day reading called it redistribution and said do-not-extend; that read used store-side sessions only, because the site-side denominator was wrongly believed unreadable. Extending the pattern to other commercial page types is now justified on evidence. Keep measuring at the STORE for revenue and at the SITE for design effect - the two moved 10% and 25% respectively over the same window.

nextPick.candidate: Weekly newsletter on the three-CTA template (shipped fc11fa2, unsent)
nextPick.rationale: Iteration 1 returned zero and is killed. Iteration 2 succeeded on conversion - 0.95% -> 7.24%, beating its 5% case - but site-wide affiliate clicks still sit at 2.87/day against a 15/day milestone, because lead-type page views more than HALVED (629 -> 304) over the same fortnight. Conversion is no longer the binding constraint; traffic is. Email is the only lever that creates visitors without waiting on the stalled crawl: the single 2026-08-12 send produced 17 sessions, and workagedleads/email measured exactly 0 in the last window because nothing was mailed. The 2026-08-31 issue is drafted and seed-verified on the new template - 12 store links against 17 site links, first at 17% page depth.

expected.basis: 17 sessions on the old one-link template x 4.3 sends/mo = 74/mo at parity, before any lift from the CTA rebuild. That alone would roughly double the 4.15/day site figure. Treat 17/send as the floor, since it was measured on a template with a single store link at 79% page depth.

alsoConsidered: Extend the hero door to other commercial page types. NOW JUSTIFIED - the earlier same-day note saying do-not-extend was based on a mis-measurement and is withdrawn. Ranked below the newsletter only because the door multiplies traffic the site is currently losing, while the newsletter supplies traffic that does not depend on the crawl.

GSC Change of Address - DONE 2026-09-01. Bill filed and passed validation for BOTH agedleadsales.com -> workagedleads.com and howtoworkleads.com -> workagedleads.com, after repeated failures in August that CLICK-LOOP.md had written off as 'Confirmed dead'. Why the retry passed is not established and should not be recorded as if it were: every redirect a validator follows is now a literal cross-domain 301 (howtoworkleads emitted a 308 until its homepage rule was switched to statusCode 301), and Google's own guidance on that error is also to wait and retry. Baseline for measuring it, captured the day of filing, 7-day rolling: agedleadsales 37 clicks / 4217 impressions / position 20.1; howtoworkleads ~4 clicks and ~600 impressions per day / position ~22; workagedleads 1 click / 338 impressions / position 65.0. Success = the two retiring properties draining into workagedleads while its position moves from 65 toward 20. Measure 2026-09-15. A flat fortnight is not failure: CoA prioritizes recrawl, it does not move rankings on our schedule, and the 301s were always doing the consolidation on their own.
Leakage recapture (63 of 149 outbound clicks). Flat since the last reading and still off-limits as removal - those links are what make the reviews independent.

kills.reason: Zero sessions from after-pricing and after-economics in 13 days. Killing the BET, not the code: the two placements stay (they cost nothing and do not harm citation value), but the statistics page is retired as a monetization target. Its readers want a number to quote, not leads to buy.
